title: Residency & retention governor: automated drift detection, safe autocorrect, and audit evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a policy-as-code 'governor' that enforces data residency and retention settings across hosted and private deployments, detects config drift, and either auto-remediates in a safe manner or produces tamper-evident audit bundles for compliance teams. This ticket covers the enforcement engine extension, drift detection scheduler and webhook model, safe autocorrect strategy (canary/dry-run/ratelimit), and automated evidence/report generation for auditors and internal security reviews.
acceptance_criteria: A policy definition format exists to express residency (region sets per customer) and retention (TTL per resource type) as code and is stored in repo 'infra/compliance-policies'
Automated scanner runs on a 15-minute cadence and flags any resource whose effective residency or retention differs from the policy
Remediation path supports two modes: dry-run (report only) and safe-autocorrect (canary + rate-limited API/terraform changes) configurable per customer and per policy

Every detection and remediation generates an immutable evidence bundle (signed manifest + resource snapshot + diff + remediation actions) uploaded to the compliance S3 bucket and surfaced in the Console audit view
Integration tests cover at least 3 drift scenarios (manual mislabel, terraform drift, cross-region replication mismatch) and assert correct remediation mode and evidence artifacts
Feature flags and RBAC controls exist so enterprise customers can opt-out of autocorrect and require human approval

risk_and_tradeoffs: Autocorrect reduces time-to-remediate but increases blast radius; mitigated via canary groups, throttling, and customer opt-outs.
Using internal policy runner avoids duplicating policy across teams but requires careful migration of existing Conftest/OPA rules.
Evidence bundles must be tamper-evident and retained for configurable retention periods; encryption and key-rotation policy needed (KMS integration).
remediation_strategy: Phase 1: Report-only mode (default) - scanner produces evidence bundles and Console alerts without changing infra.

Phase 2: Safe-autocorrect - enable for low-risk policy classes with canary rollout: apply change to 1% of impacted resources, monitor telemetry for 30 minutes, then continue in geometric ramp if no regressions.
Phase 3: Approval flow - for high-risk changes present a curated remediation plan in Console and require 2 approvers (Platform SRE + Customer Security) before applying.
Rollback: all autocorrect actions must be reversible by recording reverse operations in the evidence bundle and storing the previous resource snapshot.
evidence_format: Bundle format: {timestamp}.tar.gz contains resource_snapshot.json, policy.yaml, diff.patch, remediation_plan.json, manifest.sig
Bundles uploaded to customer-specific prefix in S3 with server-side encryption and KMS key per-tenant; manifest is signed using platform key for non-repudiation
Console will surface a signed URL pointing to the bundle and a human-readable summary (policy violated, severity, suggested action, remediation status)
qa_plan: Integration tests in CI will run a simulated drift pipeline for hosted and private environments. E2E will validate scanner detection, evidence bundle contents, remediation application, and Console UI links. Manual regression tests for customer opt-out and RBAC will be included.
